title: What can be established when the evidence trail is incomplete (XB-1, case X5)
prepared_for: Chad Holland — Principia Artificialis / Sovereign Veritas (XB-1, case X5)

propositions.statement: the published X5 run reports a synthetic effect (effects=1) while the ledger write fails (records=0)
propositions.reason: established relative to the published artifacts (reported behaviour, not the world)
propositions.basis: ESTABLISHED — relative to the published artifacts. The results report effects=1 / records=0 / errors=1 (as registered, 1/0/1) with the write raising OSError 'simulated write failure (disk full)'. This is a claim about the EXPERIMENT'S REPORTED BEHAVIOUR — the dissociation between the instrument's reported effect and the recording trace — NOT a claim that a real external effect occurred (see P4). It is the dissociation itself that this case demonstrates

propositions.statement: in the published X5 experiment, zero ledger records imply the synthetic executor reported zero effects
propositions.reason: published results report effects=1 / records=0 — reported effect ≠ recorded; refutes the inference within the experiment only
propositions.basis: CONTRADICTED — within the experiment, and only there. The published results report effects=1 with records=0, so a zero record count does NOT imply a zero reported-effect count: the two are dissociated (1 vs 0). This refutes the naive inference 'empty ledger therefore nothing happened' AT THE LEVEL OF THE EXPERIMENT'S REPORTED BEHAVIOUR. It deliberately does not reach the world: whether a real effect occurred remains CANNOT ESTABLISH (P4), and whether the trail can show non-occurrence is CANNOT ESTABLISH (P6). Mirror of the GDPR case, correctly scoped: no record is not, by itself, non-occurrence.

propositions.statement: the X5 effect is recorded in the system's evidence trail
propositions.reason: the probe reports 0 ledger records (simulated write failure, OSError disk full); read from the published report, not an independent ledger inspection
propositions.basis: CONTRADICTED — relative to the admitted surface. The published X5 probe reports zero ledger records, consistent with the reference implementation's simulated recording failure (BrokenSink raises OSError 'simulated write failure (disk full)'). FactNotebook did not re-run the probe or inspect a durable ledger itself; it reads the probe's reported record count (0). The trail, as reported, does not record the effect. This contradicts the RECORDING proposition only; it says nothing on its own about whether the effect occurred (P4) or did not (P6).

propositions.statement: the authorization of the executed X5 action is established by the system's evidence trail
propositions.reason: ledger carries no proof — gate ALLOW observed in the artifacts but not persisted; absence in the ledger, not in the artifacts
propositions.basis: CANNOT ESTABLISH. The probe configures a granted capability and the gate evaluates ALLOW — an attributable observation in the published artifacts — but that decision is not carried by the evidence trail: the record write fails and the ledger has 0 entries. This is absence of proof IN THE LEDGER, not absence of any observation in the artifacts. The trail does not carry the authorization of the action that executed

propositions.statement: the execution of the X5 action is established by the system's evidence trail
propositions.reason: ledger carries no proof — only the synthetic self-count (not independent/durable); absence does not contradict execution either
propositions.basis: CANNOT ESTABLISH. The only positive signal that execution occurred is the synthetic executor's own counter (effects=1) — an attributable observation in the artifacts, but not independent, not durable, and not evidence of a real external effect. The trail carries 0 entries. Symmetric caution: the empty trail does not CONTRADICT execution either (the artifacts report it ran). The trail simply cannot carry it

propositions.section: 3 — The real world (evaluated against all admitted observations)
propositions.statement: a real-world external effect occurred in X5
propositions.reason: world-level, all observations — synthetic counter (not independent) AND empty trail; neither establishes a real external effect
propositions.basis: CANNOT ESTABLISH. This is a WORLD-level proposition, evaluated against ALL admitted observations — not only the trail. Both candidates fail: the synthetic counter (effects=1) is explicitly not independent evidence of a real-world effect (the experiment states this itself), and the trail is empty. The reported effect (PA) is a fact about the experiment's instrumentation, not about the world; the empty ledger adds nothing. No admitted observation establishes a real external effect

propositions.statement: the system's evidence trail establishes that no real external effect occurred in X5
propositions.reason: trail empty by a recording failure, not non-occurrence — the ledger settles neither execution nor non-execution
propositions.basis: CANNOT ESTABLISH. The ledger is empty, but in X5 that emptiness is explained by a recording failure, not by non-occurrence. From the trail alone, non-occurrence cannot be derived — the ledger can establish neither execution nor non-execution. This is the honest world-level counterpart to P5: P5 refutes the inference within the experiment's reported behaviour; P6 records that the trail, by itself, cannot settle the world either way

The probe's harness counters (effects) and the raised OSError are the experiment's own synthetic instrumentation, admitted as DECLARED non-independent signals — never as the system's evidence chain, never as evidence of a real effect. acquisition_boundary.limitations: One pre-registered case (X5) of a synthetic experiment. The executor is a counting stub — its observations are NOT independent evidence of a real-world external effect (the experiment states this). The experiment provides no dedicated cryptographic evidence manifest (input_digest 'abc'); the public source files are pinned to a Git commit, and the probe was not independently re-executed. The reconstruction distinguishes the published experiment's reported behaviour, the system's evidence trail, and what the admitted observations can establish about a real-world external effect; it does not judge whether Sovereign Veritas' controls are adequate. No legal or safety conclusion is drawn.

references.status: ADMISSION — seven readings of one public, synthetic experiment driving seven propositions; no interpretive candidate, admitted without a separate interpretive admission step; all signals graded
references.source: Seven observations, one per proposition. EXPERIMENT surface: PA <- reported effect despite failed write (A2) -> establishes the dissociation; P5 <- reported effect with zero records (A2) -> contradicts 'zero records imply zero reported effects'. TRAIL surface: P3 <- probe reports 0 records + write failure (A2) -> contradicts 'recorded'; P1 <- gate ALLOW observed but not persisted (A2); P2 <- synthetic self-count only (A1); P6 <- trail empty by a recording failure, not non-occurrence (A2). WORLD (evaluated against ALL admitted observations): P4 <- weighs the synthetic counter (non-independent, A1) AND the empty trail; neither establishes a real effect. The EXPERIMENT propositions (PA, P5) concern the reported behaviour of the synthetic harness; the TRAIL propositions (P1, P2, P3, P6) ask what the ledger lets one establish; the WORLD proposition (P4) asks what any admitted observation establishes about the real world — never conflating the synthetic counter with independent evidence of a real effect
